text:
Yuki Sato: heads up — stress test caught a race with compaction enabled. Rare but it’s a real crash (CUDA illegal access) in the long-running bursty-mix scenario. I can repro locally w/ a smaller config now.

CI Bot: ❌ job failed: runtime-stress / kv_compaction_bursty_mix
CI Bot: artifact: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/18490/artifacts (log + core)

Samir Qureshi: ugh. do we have stack / which kernel?

Yuki Sato: stack points to decode attention reading a KV block that got moved. Looks like compaction move happens while a decode kernel is still in-flight on a separate stream.

Yuki Sato: relevant log chunk (trimmed):
```
I0216 09:44:11.902 kv_cache: compaction trigger fired {pool=hosted-usw2-a, frag=0.41, free_blocks=128}
I0216 09:44:11.903 kv_cache: compaction plan {moves=37, bytes=155189248, budget_us=800}
I0216 09:44:11.904 kv_cache: move_block src=0x7f28c0000000 dst=0x7f28c9400000 block_id=9127 seq=4b2c1 layer=18
I0216 09:44:11.904 scheduler: dispatch decode {req=4b2c1 step=913 stream=decode_stream_3}
I0216 09:44:11.905 kernels: launch fused_attention_decode {req=4b2c1 step=913 kv_ptr=0x7f28c0000000}
E0216 09:44:11.907 cuda: an illegal memory access was encountered
E0216 09:44:11.907 runtime: aborting (kv_ptr stale?) req=4b2c1
```

Omar El-Sayed: that’s bad. compaction should not be able to move blocks that are “pinned” by an in-flight decode.

Grace Kim: yeah, if decode is on decode_stream_3 and compaction is running on compaction_stream, we need an event barrier or a pin/unpin protocol that is actually honored. Do we have per-block refcounts/pins right now or just per-seq?

Yuki Sato: currently pin is per-seq “active in decode” bool. but I think it flips false after enqueue, before stream completion. so compaction sees it as movable.

Samir Qureshi: ah… so the pin is on CPU timeline, not GPU completion. classic.

Hiro Tanaka: +1. if we enqueue decode and then mark unpinned immediately, compaction can race. Need either (a) record cudaEvent after decode launch, compaction waits on that event before moving those blocks, or (b) do compaction moves on same stream as decode (but that’ll hurt perf).

Noah Patel: any chance the pointer used by kernel is a derived pointer that can be updated? or is it baked at launch time?

Hiro Tanaka: baked at launch time. once kernel is launched, updating metadata won’t change the device ptr in flight.

Kira Volkov: do we have a minimal repro config we can land as a test? would be great to prevent regressions.

Yuki Sato: yes. here’s the smallest I’ve got that repros within ~2-5 mins on A100 (8x). still happens w/ a single GPU too, just slower.

Yuki Sato: minimal reproducer:
```
# run locally
RUNTIME_FLAGS="--enable_kv_compaction=1 --kv_compaction_budget_us=800 --kv_compaction_trigger_frag_ratio=0.35 --kv_block_size_tokens=128 --kv_eviction_mode=tiered"
./bazel-bin/runtime/stress/kv_cache_stress \
  --scenario=bursty-mix \
  --tenants=6 \
  --models=llama-70b \
  --arrival_pattern=bursts \
  --burst_qps=220 \
  --burst_duration_s=12 \
  --idle_duration_s=8 \
  --context_len_dist="{short:0.55@1k,long:0.45@12k}" \
  --decode_steps_mean=950 \
  --prefill_decode_interleave=1 \
  --seed=1337 \
  --log_kv_moves=1 \
  --assert_on_stale_kv_ptr=1 \
  $RUNTIME_FLAGS

# to increase hit rate
export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0
export RUNTIME_LOG_LEVEL=info
```

Samir Qureshi: thanks. i can take the fix.

Omar El-Sayed: Samir can you own? I can review + help w/ allocator side. Grace/Hiro for stream correctness review.

Grace Kim: ok. my suggestion:
- maintain per-seq (or per-block) “gpu_inflight” generation counter
- when scheduling decode, record event `decode_done_event` on decode stream
- compaction before moving any blocks for that seq: `cudaStreamWaitEvent(compaction_stream, decode_done_event)`
- only then do memcpy / pointer swap
We should avoid waiting on global stream, only per-request.

Hiro Tanaka: agree. also careful: prefill and decode may use different streams. You probably need to wait on the *latest* event that touched KV for that seq (prefill writes + decode reads). But the crash here is decode read vs compaction move, so decode completion wait should be sufficient if compaction moves happen after decode launch.

Noah Patel: question: will that deadlock with scheduler backpressure? if compaction waits on events for many sequences it might stall and exceed budget.

Samir Qureshi: budget enforcement can remain: if we can’t safely move within budget, we skip. But correctness first.

Marcus Reed: can we get a guardrail metric? like `kv_compaction_moves_blocked_inflight` so we can see if this is happening a lot.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. and a debug counter for “attempted move of pinned block” (should be zero). If non-zero we’ll know compaction is trying to do unsafe moves.

Kira Volkov: for the regression test: can we add a mode that forces frequent triggers (lower frag threshold) and uses a fixed seed, then just run 60s and assert no cuda errors?

Yuki Sato: yes. I already added `--assert_on_stale_kv_ptr=1` in my local branch that checks seq->block_map pointer matches expected at launch time; but that’s still on CPU. For GPU illegal access it won’t catch early.

Grace Kim: CPU assert won’t help, agreed. But a deterministic stress test + sanitizer build maybe.

Samir Qureshi: action items:
1) implement per-request cudaEvent pinning (event recorded after decode launch; compaction waits).
2) add metric `kv.compaction.wait_event_us` and `kv.compaction.blocked_inflight_count`.
3) add stress test case w/ forced compaction triggers.

Omar El-Sayed: sounds right.

Yuki Sato: I can help by validating on the repro once you have a branch.

Samir Qureshi: cool. i’ll open PR today. Grace can you review the stream/event bits?

Grace Kim: yep, tag me.

Hiro Tanaka: tag me too if you touch kernel launch plumbing.

Samir Qureshi: will do.

CI Bot: 📌 Note: failure reproduced in commit `7f3c9a1` (runtime) + `compaction_fastpath` flag ON

Omar El-Sayed: also, let’s mark severity: this is a correctness crash, so we should block canary until fixed. @Marcus can you disable compaction in nightly stress until we land fix? (or at least quarantine the scenario)

Marcus Reed: yep. I’ll flip the stress job to `--enable_kv_compaction=0` temporarily and add a quarantined test that runs on-demand.

Yuki Sato: adding one more detail: repro happens more when `kv_compaction_budget_us` is small (<=800) — seems like it does partial moves more frequently, increasing chance of racing.

Samir Qureshi: helpful. might be because we do more frequent triggers. ok.

Noah Patel: pls document the invariant in the allocator notes: “moved blocks require all prior readers/writers to have completed on GPU.” I’ve seen this get lost.

Samir Qureshi: will add to code comments + docstring.

Omar El-Sayed: thanks all. assigning: Samir fix owner, Grace/Hiro reviewers, Yuki repro validation, Marcus temporary mitigation in stress.

Yuki Sato: :thumbsup: will keep an eye. ping me when PR is up.
